themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, a 2300% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 0.1 complaints per week, suggesting a potential widespread indoor environmental hazard affecting multiple buildings in Bayside-Douglaston.
evidence: 3 indoor air quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
Highest statistical severity spike in dataset, indicating sudden cluster rather than gradual trend
531 building permits filed over 90 days (345 alterations, 61 major renovations) may be disturbing indoor air systems or creating construction-related contamination
reporting_angles: Identify the 3 buildings with complaints; interview residents about symptoms (mold, odors, respiratory issues); check if recent renovations or HVAC work triggered problems

Contact NYC Department of Health to determine if indoor air quality cluster has been flagged; investigate whether complaints correlate with specific building types (schools, senior centers, residential)

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Team Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK, a 567% spike from the 0.8 weekly average, indicating potential code enforcement or building compliance actions concentrated in a short timeframe.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.13)
SPIT handles illegal conversions and unpermitted building uses—aligns with CB budget request history on addressing illegal conversions
175 active DOB alteration permits (ALT-CO category) suggest building modifications that may trigger compliance investigations
reporting_angles: FOIL request to DOB for SPIT inspection locations and findings THIS WEEK; determine if targeting specific neighborhoods or building types
Interview CB411 members about illegal conversion complaints; cross-reference with community board meeting minutes and standing agenda items on this issue

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 967% increase over the 8-week baseline (0.4 per week), suggesting potential chemical, asbestos, or lead-adjacent contamination events that may still be unresolved.
evidence: 4 hazardous materials complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.49)
Lead complaints also spiked to 7 two weeks ago (195% increase, z-score: 3.8), suggesting contamination cluster may include lead-based hazards
Dumpster complaints UP 300% (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 avg), potentially tied to improper hazmat disposal
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and Sanitation to identify which facilities/sites generated hazmat complaints 2 weeks ago; determine remediation status
Interview residents near complaint addresses about exposure symptoms; check if schools or senior centers (budget priority areas) were affected by hazmat incidents

themes_detail.label: Lead Contamination Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints jumped to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 195% increase over the 8-week average of 2.4 per week, raising concerns about lead in water systems, paint, or soil that may affect vulnerable populations including children in this aging residential district.
evidence: 7 lead complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.8)
Water System complaints remain elevated at 367 total over 90 days, suggesting ongoing water infrastructure issues that could leach lead from aging pipes
Community Board has standing request for DEP capital funding, indicating long-unresolved water/environmental infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine which buildings/blocks reported lead 2 weeks ago and whether it was water-based, paint-based, or soil contamination; request lead testing results
Interview families with young children about lead exposure concerns; cross-reference with school health records if available; identify whether complaints concentrated in older housing stock

themes_detail.label: Dead Tree Crisis & Elevator Failures
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints doubled to 14 LAST WEEK (96% spike from 7.1 weekly average), and elevator complaints jumped to 3 (700% spike from 0.4 avg), suggesting combined infrastructure decay across two different building systems.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 14 last week vs. 7.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.62)
Elevator complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77)
Community Board budget history includes park/building/access improvement requests and park/amenity expansion—suggests aging public infrastructure is chronic concern
reporting_angles: Map tree complaints to specific parks or streets in CB411; interview Parks Department about removal/replacement timeline and budget constraints
Identify the 3 buildings with elevator failures; determine if they are residential or commercial; check if complaints linked to deferred maintenance in rent-stabilized housing
